key_insight: A set of case studies shows that advanced Gemini-based LLMs (e.g., Gemini Deep Think) can meaningfully accelerate scientific workflows by collaborating with researchers on routine and some expert-level mathematical tasks, revealing practical techniques to improve model–researcher collaboration.
problem_solved: Clarifies how LLMs can be integrated into scientific research and addresses the uncertainty about their ability to contribute to novel, expert-level mathematical discovery and everyday research tasks.
method: Curated case studies where researchers collaborated with Gemini-based models on domain problems, documenting prompts, iterations, and outcomes.
Extraction of common techniques and workflows (e.g., iterative prompting, tool use, stepwise verification) that improved model usefulness and reliability.
Qualitative analysis of successes, failure modes, and practical guidelines for deploying advanced LLMs in research pipelines.
impact: Provides actionable workflows and cautionary insights for AI/ML practitioners looking to integrate LLMs into scientific pipelines, helping teams leverage models for faster hypothesis testing, derivations, and routine analysis while managing risks.
visual_elements: Human–AI collaboration flowchart showing iterative prompting, model draft, researcher verification, and refinement loop
Bar or radar chart comparing common techniques (iterative prompting, chain-of-thought, tool use, verification) vs. effectiveness across case studies
Annotated case-study timeline highlighting problem → model interaction → outcome and key interventions
Icon set for best-practice checklist (prompt design, verification steps, tool integration, risk controls)
paper_title: Accelerating Scientific Research with Gemini: Case Studies and Common Techniques
paper_authors: David P. Woodruff, Vincent Cohen-Addad, Lalit Jain, Jieming Mao, Song Zuo
